speakers: Peter Oppenheimer (chief global equity strategist, Goldman Sachs)
summary: October 2022 interview: Oppenheimer frames the 2022 bear market as cyclical (inflation-driven rate rises) rather than structural, lists conditions for a market bottom, and explains the rate-driven growth-vs-value reversal. Conclusions: dollar strong near term but PPP-overvalued, commodities in a super cycle, higher cost of capital means lower returns and more alpha.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: it's been triggered by Rising inflation as a result of supply-side shots
claims.claim: The 2022 downturn is unusual: it is triggered by supply-side inflation while labor markets stay very strong, with many economies already below trend or near recession.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: so that means that while there may well be an economic downturn it may not trigger the kind of negative Spirals and Vicious Cycles that we've seen in some of the other downturns in the past
claims.claim: Healthy private-sector balance sheets (low corporate debt, strong banks after tougher regulation, decent household savings) mean the downturn may not trigger negative spirals as in past recessions.
claims.indicator: corporate debt, bank capital, household savings

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: we are going through a difficult cycle weak economic growth higher inflation and that means higher interest rates and weaker asset markets
claims.claim: Weak growth with higher inflation brings higher rates and weaker asset markets.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: something we haven't really seen since the 1970s many of the inflationary problems that we're seeing at the moment are as a result of Supply shots
claims.claim: Inflation comes from both strong post-pandemic demand and supply shocks (energy, labor, mismatched supply), the latter not seen since the 1970s.
claims.testable: partly - supply vs demand decomposition possible

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: inflation eroded the value of many Financial assets and in real terms they did very very badly
claims.claim: Low growth with high inflation and rising rates (the 1970s) is the worst combination for financial assets in real terms.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: the speed of the change of prices and interest rates coming from these very low historically record low levels which is having quite a big impact on financial assets
claims.claim: Both the level and the speed of rate rises from record lows (a quarter of government bonds had negative yields a year earlier, now US 10-year about 4%) hit risky assets such as equities.
claims.indicator: 10-year yield, rate of change in yields
claims.conditions: rate shock from very low levels
claims.testable: yes - rate changes vs asset returns

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: demand recovered pretty quickly Supply didn't recover as quickly inflation started to rise
claims.claim: After the GFC central banks used zero rates and QE, and in the pandemic more money printing and fiscal support; demand recovered faster than supply and inflation rose.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: for a long time the central banks thought all of this would be very temporary
claims.claim: Central banks long called inflation transitory, giving up the language only at the start of 2022, so they were slow to react.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: they're prepared to raise rates sufficiently to contain inflation even if that means that we'll see an economic downturn or a recession
claims.claim: In 2022 the central bank priority shifted to a whatever-it-takes fight against inflation, accepting recession risk.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: that sort of evolution of um of of the perception of central banks and how they're dealing with inflation that spooked investors
claims.claim: The shift in central bank stance, not inflation alone, caused the summer 2022 market sell-off as investors feared tightening and growth impact.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: now people talk about Tara there are alternatives um to equities
claims.claim: With rates, bond yields (3.5-4%) and real yields now positive, TINA has become TARA: there are alternatives to equities, so diversification across assets makes sense.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: the near-term pressure on Equity prices is still probably downwards
claims.claim: Rising real yields mean near-term downward pressure on equities.
claims.testable: yes - real yield vs equity returns

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: valuations typically get to quite low levels at a point where Equity markets trough and rebound
claims.claim: A recession bear market usually falls about 30% and troughs at low valuations; in 2022 most markets were down 20 to mid-20s%, so one condition for a base was not met.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: equities do start to recover while economic conditions are weak because investors start to anticipate a recovery before it's actually apparent
claims.claim: Equities recover once the rate of growth deterioration slows, before the economy improves, because investors anticipate recovery.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: when interest rates Peak and inflation Peaks that equities start to recover
claims.claim: Equity bear markets usually end when interest rates and inflation peak.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: the US of course the biggest Equity Market in the world uh has uh only just really got back to kind of average valuations having been well above average valuations for a very long time
claims.claim: US equities had only just returned to average valuations after a long period well above average supported by low rates, so more adjustment may be needed.

claims.speaker: Simon (host)
claims.quote: in the last 96 years we've had nine recessions and 73 of the largest U.S Equity drawdowns of course happened with recessions
claims.claim: Over 96 years there were nine recessions and 73% of the largest US equity drawdowns coincided with recessions.

claims.speaker: Simon (host)
claims.quote: in the 70s the USP got to sort of 12 times in the inflationary environment that we had then
claims.claim: In the inflationary 1970s the S&P fell to about 12 times earnings, a warning that averages are deceptive.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: typically you would see Equity markets fall about 60 from Peak to trough but these are in conditions where you've seen a major asset price bubble
claims.claim: Structural downturns (1929, Japan late 1980s, 2008) involve an equity and real estate bubble with heavy private leverage and a banking crisis, with equities falling about 60%.
claims.indicator: asset bubble, private debt, bank crisis

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: the prices and equities are just very quickly usually down about 30 percent uh but then uh because the broad underlying cycle is reasonably healthy economically the recovery is pretty fast
claims.claim: Event-driven downturns (wars, commodity crises, the pandemic) cause quick falls of about 30% and fast recovery when the underlying cycle is healthy.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: usually late in an economic expansion you know you get some inflationary pressures building up that forces the central bank to raise interest rates and that rise in interest rates triggers an expectation of an economic downturn
claims.claim: Cyclical bear markets arise late in an expansion when inflation forces the central bank to raise rates and investors expect downturn and falling profits.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: they don't tend to happen in a straight line you you tend to get fours and then rallies and falls again
claims.claim: Cyclical bear markets usually fall around 30%, occur with bear market rallies over about two years (such as summer 2022).

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: we're probably in one of these cyclical downturns I don't think it will be significantly deeper partly because of these private sector balances
claims.claim: The 2022 bear market is cyclical rather than structural, not deeper than usual because no broad bubbles and banks have low leverage.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: governments capping at those prices for households and that's again won't prevent a downturn but may moderate the scale of what might have otherwise happened
claims.claim: Government energy price caps in Europe may moderate the downturn without preventing it.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: things that were seen to be high growth did very well and things that were if you like very value orientated lower value companies more mature industries did very badly
claims.claim: After the GFC returns were bifurcated: high-growth equities outperformed value and mature industries in the 2010s.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: nominal GDP so GDP including inflation was very weak so investors were prepared to pay more for anything they were convinced to grow
claims.claim: Weak nominal GDP made investors pay up for growth after the GFC.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: interest rates towards zero had a bigger positive impact on the valuation of higher growth companies than um slower growth companies
claims.claim: Falling rates have a bigger valuation effect on long-duration growth companies, so they derate more when rates rise.
claims.direction: long growth when rates fall; short growth when rates rise
claims.testable: yes - rate sensitivity of growth stocks

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: became seen as value traps they were cheap in valuation terms but they were suffering very weak growth or no growth and perhaps having to cut dividends
claims.claim: Mature industries after the GFC (commodity falls, sovereign and banking crises in Europe) were value traps: cheap but without growth.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: that simple moniker of growth versus value those sort of simple labels are not really very adequate or useful labels to be using anymore
claims.claim: Growth versus value labels are no longer useful as each has split into sub-groups.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: unprofitable growth companies you know high-tech uh more speculative types of companies which were seen very high valuations up until about a year ago having derated very sharply
claims.claim: Unprofitable high-tech growth stocks derated sharply as rates and cost of capital rose, while profitable mature growth did relatively well.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: those sort of value areas that are closest to the sources of inflation so things like energy stocks and Mining and materials uh who are able to pass on higher costs they've actually done very well
claims.claim: Within value, cyclicals fell on recession worries while energy, mining and materials, which pass on costs, outperformed in the inflation shock.
claims.direction: long energy and materials; avoid cyclicals

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: have a bit of a mixture between quality strong balance sheets relatively defensive growth and very low valued um commodity related parts of markets
claims.claim: Goldman's 2022 recommended mix: quality balance sheets, defensive growth and low-valued commodity-related stocks.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: much more agnostic to the factors say growth versus value and much more Diversified both in geographical exposure and sector and style exposure
claims.claim: Going forward be agnostic to growth versus value and diversify across geography, sector and style.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: that means less opportunity for valuations to go up it probably means lower returns but it means much more idiosyncratic returns
claims.claim: Without falling rates there is less valuation upside, lower index returns and more idiosyncratic returns, so stock selection and alpha matter more.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: there is a tendency to seek safe havens and the dollar and its uh Reserve currency status makes it quite a defensive currency to hold
claims.claim: The dollar rose because of safe-haven demand in an uncertain world given its reserve status.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: the U.S federal reserves the central bank has been raising interest rates more quickly and more aggressively than many other central banks around the world
claims.claim: The Fed's faster tightening created a large rate differential that attracts investors to the dollar.
claims.indicator: US vs foreign policy rate differential

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: that has gone up close to record high levels or at least the record highs that we saw back in the mid 1980s
claims.claim: The trade-weighted dollar was near the mid-1980s record high.

claims.speaker: Simon (host)
claims.quote: next stop is parity in fact next stop was 240
claims.claim: Dollar strength is cyclical: in 1985 sterling-dollar was 1.05 and a trader forecast parity, but it later reached 2.40.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: as other central banks raise rates the relative strength of the dollar should should start to ease and we think that would be true over the next you know year and Beyond
claims.claim: The dollar should ease as other central banks raise rates and uncertainty fades, with no collapse and still strong in the short term.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: over a very long periods of time there should be some relationship with what's called purchasing power parity
claims.claim: On purchasing power parity the dollar is overvalued, so long-term mean reversion toward PPP is expected.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: about 75 of the revenues of UK ftse 100 companies come from outside of the UK it's one of the most Global indices in the world
claims.claim: The FTSE 100 is not a UK-economy proxy: about 75% of revenues are foreign and about 50% of dividends are in dollars, so weak sterling helps it.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: the government's new policy has been to add a fiscal stimulus through tax cuts to this cocktail of of issues which is seems to be at odds with the bank of England's attempt to slow the economy to contain inflation
claims.claim: UK fiscal stimulus conflicting with Bank of England tightening spooked markets and sterling.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: it trades at around uh you know PE a price earnings ratio about nine times that's much much cheaper than say the US
claims.claim: The UK equity market trades at about 9 times earnings, cheap partly due to energy and mining weight.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: the more domestically exposed parts of the UK Market um you know have suffered much more because they are more geared to the economy
claims.claim: The UK index fell only about 5% in 2022 versus S&P about -20%, yet UK domestic stocks fell about 40%, so dispersion tracks global versus domestic exposure.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: many companies in the UK will be attractive uh potential um buying opportunities for foreign companies
claims.claim: Weak sterling and cheap valuations make UK companies targets for foreign and private equity buyers.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: pushing inflation up even in Germany which has been you know historically very low inflation anchor if you like uh you'll see inflation of over 10 at the moment
claims.claim: European gas prices after the Ukraine war pushed German inflation above 10%, forcing the ECB to hike despite weak growth.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: it's creating some tension in terms of the priorities and the obligations that the central bank has to contain inflation on the one hand but maintain you know Financial stability on the other
claims.claim: ECB rate rises raise interest costs for indebted countries such as Italy, creating tension between inflation control and financial stability.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: is now taking on renewed urgency because of the security issues
claims.claim: Europe's energy transition gains urgency, building renewable infrastructure that can later generate jobs and growth, though costly.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: in periods of higher inflation which means higher interest rates which typically would be a negative for gov Bond markets and equities uh Commodities often Thrive
claims.claim: Commodities are driven by current supply and demand, not future expectations, so they diversify bonds and equities in inflationary periods and are real assets.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: we're in a sort of secular super cycle for for many Commodities because you've had long periods of under investment in commodity infrastructure and exploration
claims.claim: Under-investment (weak post-GFC demand, low prices, ESG reluctance to fund traditional energy) set up a secular commodity super cycle.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: you can't do that without having more copper and copper means mining copper to to extract that material to facilitate that transition
claims.claim: Electrification for net zero requires much more copper, supporting prices.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: we're moving into an era where the cost of capital is going to be higher
claims.claim: A higher cost of capital after the artificial post-GFC low-rate era means lower returns.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: the shifts in geopolitics and the moves towards decarbonization are also going to mean less globalization and a bit more regionalization
claims.claim: Geopolitics and decarbonization mean less globalization and more regional production of food, chips and batteries.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: that will incentivize companies to invest in becoming more efficient by spending money on Energy Efficiency by investing in machines and uh uh artificial intelligence
claims.claim: Higher energy and labor costs push firms to invest in efficiency, automation and AI, which could lift productivity.

claims.speaker: Peter Oppenheimer
claims.quote: as governments shift their priorities and there's more demand for increasing spending on defense and also decarbonization
claims.claim: Spending on defense and decarbonization will require physical infrastructure, raising costs but creating growth and investment opportunities.
